# Bible Buddy Chapter Notes — Rewrite Progress Log

Tracks the chapter-by-chapter rewrite of Bible Reader study notes (section
cards / phrase cards) to match the Genesis 1-40 gold-standard voice, per
`.claude/skills/write-chapter-notes/SKILL.md`.

Total chapters in the Bible: 1,189.
Already at gold-standard quality before this log started: Genesis 1-40 (40 chapters).
Chapters logged in this table so far: 818 (as of Isaiah 66, the sixty sixth and final chapter of Isaiah; the entire books of Genesis through Isaiah are now complete. All of Jeremiah through Malachi and all of Matthew through Revelation still carry only their original auto-generated legacy placeholder wiring and are not yet counted as done). Note: Isaiah 58 and 59 are complete and wired (see `data/bible-notes-progress-log.json`) but their rows were never appended to this table by the runs that finished them; that gap predates this entry and is left as found rather than backfilled here.

Psalms 119 is a 22 stanza acrostic, one stanza per letter of the Hebrew alphabet from Aleph to Tau, each stanza exactly 8 verses, built almost entirely around eight overlapping Hebrew synonyms for God's word: law (torah), testimonies (eduth), way (derek), precepts (piqqudim), statutes (choq), commandments (mitzvah), judgments (mishpat), and word (dabar). Split into 22 sections, one per stanza, with 180 phrase cards total (about one per verse, deliberately lighter than the usual ~2x target given how repetitive the acrostic's own vocabulary is by design; each of the eight synonym words was defined in full on its first appearance in Aleph/Beth and referenced rather than re-defined afterward so later cards could focus on what was actually new in that verse). Covered: the acrostic form and the eight synonym words (Aleph, vv1-8); hiding God's word in the heart in a culture with no personal scripture copies (Beth, vv9-16); the proud as a recurring antagonist first named, and princes sitting in official council against him (Gimel, vv17-24); "cleaveth unto the dust" as a mourning idiom for despair versus the same root word used positively later for "stuck unto" God (Daleth, vv25-32); coveting reversing the earlier riches comparison, and "vanity" as empty/idol language (He, vv33-40); law and liberty paired on purpose, and speaking boldly before kings after princes had judged him (Vau, vv41-48); "judgments of old" recalling the exodus, and statutes turned into songs during a "pilgrimage" that echoes the earlier stranger language (Zain, vv49-56); "portion" as Levitical inheritance language, and midnight prayer vigils (Cheth, vv57-64); the explicit claim that affliction was genuinely good for him and taught him what comfort could not (Teth, vv65-72); being fashioned like clay by a potter, and suffering explicitly named an act of God's own faithfulness (Jod, vv73-80); "bottle in the smoke" as a wineskin dried out by hearth smoke, and honest, undisguised complaint to God (Caph, vv81-88); God's word "settled in heaven" beyond the reach of any earthly crisis, and nature itself pictured as obedient (Lamed, vv89-96); surpassing teachers and elders through meditation rather than formal status, and scripture "sweeter than honey" (Mem, vv97-104); the famous "lamp unto my feet" explained as a small ancient oil lamp lighting only the next step, not a floodlight, plus night watches and a formal sworn oath (Nun, vv105-112); "vain thoughts" as double mindedness, hiding place and shield as war imagery, and the dross/refining metaphor for the wicked (Samech, vv113-120); "surety" as a legal guarantor for debt, and the bold "it is time for thee LORD to work" (Ain, vv121-128); "the entrance of thy words" as a door or scroll opening light even to "the simple," and panting like a runner for God's commandments (Pe, vv129-136); the dross/refining image doubled back into "thy word is very pure," and being "small and despised" in an honor-shame society (Tzaddi, vv137-144); "prevented the dawning of the morning" using the archaic sense of prevented (to come before, not stop), and ancient night watches (Qoph, vv145-152); ## Pace notes

- 2026-07-24: First session included voice calibration (drafts revised twice
  before Genesis 41 was approved). Actual writing pace once the voice is
  locked in should be faster than this session's — treat day 1 as an outlier,
  not a baseline.

## Voice standard (locked in 2026-07-24)

- Short, plain sentences. Avoid words like "scarcity" — aim for a 5th/6th
  grade reading level.
- Explain the *meaning* of a phrase, not a recap of what already happened in
  the verse (reader already read it).
- Favor historical/cultural grounding: what would this have meant to the
  original audience, and why (Egyptian customs, geography, real KJV word
  definitions), over generic inspirational commentary.
- Full phrase coverage per section — do not skip verses/phrases for pacing.
  Genesis 41 sections ran 5-9 verses each with 2-6 phrase cards.
- No `➡️` transition lines (dropped from the original skill spec per user
  feedback on 2026-07-24) — cards end after the emoji bullets.
- Reference implementation: `lib/genesisFortyOneSource.ts`.
